name: 28BYJ-48 stepper motor (5 V)
description: 28BYJ-48 5 V unipolar geared stepper motor: four 50 Ohm half windings on a red common, a permanent-magnet rotor with 32 full steps a turn geared 63.684:1 (2037.9 full steps an output turn, 64 half steps of 5.625 degrees a rotor turn), the rotor integrated as a mass with detent torque and gearbox friction so it follows up to the data sheet's pull-in rate and misses steps or stalls beyond it. Usually driven by a ULN2003 board; red open, it works bipolar from an H-bridge.

pins.name: BLUE
pins.doc: Half winding at 270 degrees (with yellow one winding); connector pin 1, the ULN2003 board's IN1

pins.name: PINK
pins.doc: Half winding at 180 degrees (with orange one winding); connector pin 2, IN2

pins.name: YELLOW
pins.doc: Half winding at 90 degrees; connector pin 3, IN3

pins.name: ORANGE
pins.doc: Half winding at 0 degrees; connector pin 4, IN4

pins.name: RED
pins.doc: The windings' common: +5 V for unipolar drive (a ULN2003 sinking the leads); left open the windings work bipolar

supply.doc: The voltage a logic 1 stands for on red and the leads under the functional and timed policies (the analog nets' own voltages under the electrical policy)

resistance.doc: A half winding's resistance (the data sheet's 50 Ohm, +-7%)

ratio.doc: The gearbox's reduction (32/9 x 22/11 x 26/9 x 31/10; the data sheet rounds it to 64)

inputs.name: load
inputs.doc: Torque on the output shaft against the positive direction (an arm's weight, a brake)

outputs.name: angle
outputs.doc: The output shaft's angle from the start, positive in the direction the data sheet's sequence (orange, yellow, pink, blue) turns it

outputs.name: steps
outputs.doc: The rotor's position in full steps from the start

outputs.name: rpm
outputs.doc: The output shaft's speed, revolutions a minute

functional.claims: Four 50 Ohm, 3 mH half windings on red, energised while a lead is below red (bipolar with red open); a permanent-magnet rotor of 8 pole pairs, 32 full steps a turn, with detent torque, inertia, gearbox friction and damping integrated in 20 us steps, so it follows up to about 650 full steps a second from standstill (the data sheet's in-traction above 600 Hz) and about 1200 with a ramp (out-traction above 1000 Hz), and misses steps or stalls faster; geared 63.684:1, 2037.9 full steps an output turn; opposite halves together cancel; the lead voltages are logic levels at `supply`.
omissions: the gears' backlash
the gears' self-locking against a load that back-drives the shaft (the data sheet's 600 to 1200 gf.cm friction torque)
the windings' pull on the leads goes to the 5 V rail, not to red's own voltage
the coupling between the two halves of a winding (each decays alone)
the supply current drawn on the nets
heating (the data sheet's rise below 40 K)
the sound it makes

electrical.claims: Each lead is pulled up through its 50 Ohm half winding (to the 5 V rail), so a driver's saturation voltage shows; the voltages across the halves are the analog nets', sampled 5 us after a lead changes and every millisecond while the rotor moves; the behaviour is the Lua model's.
